title: The Transit Allowance Added to the Settlement Clock on an Auto Loan
content:
A transit allowance is added to the span the anchor gives when a loan of the Auto Loans line is settled in full. Its size is read from the borrower's Personal Credit Cards account.

**0 days** where the borrower's card carries at least 25000 unredeemed reward points and at least 12 card purchases have posted in the last three months.

**1 day** where that card carries at least 5000 unredeemed reward points and at least 3 card purchases have posted in the last three months, while either those points fall short of 25000 or those purchases fall short of 12.

**3 days** for every other borrower.

## The three allowances on one span

| Unredeemed reward points | Card purchases posted in the last three months | Transit allowance | Days the clock runs on a span of 30 |
|---|---|---|---|
| At least 25000 | At least 12 | 0 days | 30 |
| At least 5000, either reading short of the row above | At least 3, either reading short of the row above | 1 day | 31 |
| Any other reading | Any other reading | 3 days | 33 |

## What each reading counts

The points reading is the unredeemed reward balance on the borrower's active card account in the Personal Credit Cards line. The purchase reading counts purchases posted to that card over the three months ending on the day of the settlement, not their amounts.

## The allowance at the edge of each row

A card carrying exactly 25000 points with 11 purchases takes 1 day. A card carrying 4999 points takes 3 days whatever its purchase count. A card carrying 25000 points with 12 purchases takes 0 days, and the clock then runs only for the days the anchor gives.
